# Kourovka Problem 9.62 (the variety generated by block lattices)

The proposition that the variety of lattices generated by the block lattices of all groups contains every finite lattice: every lattice identity $p = q$ (terms in variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$ built from $\vee$ and $\wedge$) that holds in $C(G)$ for every group $G$, under every assignment of blocks to the variables, holds in every finite lattice. The blocks of a group $G$ are the empty set and the cosets $gN$ of normal subgroups $N$; ordered by inclusion they form the block lattice $C(G)$, with meet the intersection and join of two blocks the intersection of all blocks containing their union.

Source: E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 9.62 (D. M. Smirnov).
